name: QGIS
description: The free desktop GIS used across the course. Install the long-term release for coursework.
about: QGIS is a complete desktop GIS: it reads nearly every vector and raster format through GDAL, edits data with snapping and topology tools, runs analysis through its Processing toolbox, and produces print-quality maps from its layout composer. It is the software most Pakistani employers now run alongside or instead of ArcGIS, and it is the one you can keep using after graduation without a licence.

It works as a host for other open-source engines. GRASS, SAGA and GDAL algorithms appear inside the Processing toolbox, so one install gives you several hundred tools. Python is built in through the console and plugin system, and the plugin repository adds things like Semi-Automatic Classification for imagery, QuickMapServices for basemaps and DataPlotly for charts.

Two versions are published at any time. The long-term release (LTR) changes only for bug fixes for a year and is what the course, the tutorials and most organisations use. The latest release has newer features and more surprises. Install the LTR unless a tutorial tells you otherwise.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; macOS 12 or later; or any current Linux distribution
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended for raster work
About 2 GB of disk space for the install, plus space for your data
A graphics driver with OpenGL 2.0 support; integrated graphics are fine
On Windows use the standalone installer (.msi), not OSGeo4W, unless you need a custom GDAL build

name: ArcGIS Pro
description: Esri's current desktop GIS. Installers for 3.7 and 3.6 are mirrored for students who hold a licence through the institute.
about: ArcGIS Pro is the 64-bit successor to ArcMap and the desktop half of Esri's platform. It combines 2D and 3D mapping in one project, uses a ribbon interface, and runs geoprocessing tools from the same toolbox you can call from Python through the arcpy library. Projects hold maps, layouts, toolboxes and connections together in a single .aprx file.

Its strengths are the depth of the geoprocessing library, the cartographic and layout tools, the tight connection to ArcGIS Online for sharing web maps, and the extensions for network, spatial statistics, image analysis and 3D. Most government departments, NESPAK and the large consultancies in Pakistan run it, and the Esri certificate is the one job adverts name.
Choose 3.7 unless a course or a plugin you depend on requires 3.6. Both need a licence before they will open. The installer is the same one Esri distributes; nothing here unlocks it.
requirements: Windows 11 or Windows 10 (version 22H2 or later), 64-bit; Windows Server 2019 or later also supported
Processor with at least four cores; eight or more recommended for imagery and 3D
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended, 32 GB for large rasters and scene layers
32 GB of free disk space, SSD strongly recommended
DirectX 12 capable graphics card with 4 GB of dedicated memory; 8 GB for 3D scenes
Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime 8, which the installer prompts for if missing
Screen resolution of 1024 x 768 or higher; a 1080p display is realistic for the ribbon
licensing: The institute holds an education licence. Sign in with a named-user account on the university's ArcGIS Online organisation, or ask the GIS lab for a single-use authorisation file. If you have no account, request one from the lab coordinator with your registration number. Esri also offers a free Learn ArcGIS trial for course MOOCs, which lasts for the duration of the course.

name: ArcGIS Desktop (ArcMap) 10.8.2
description: The retired 32-bit ArcMap, still used in older labs and by some departments. Mirror coming; use ArcGIS Pro for new work.
about: ArcGIS Desktop is the previous generation of Esri's desktop software: ArcMap for 2D mapping and editing, ArcCatalog for data management, ArcScene and ArcGlobe for 3D. It is 32-bit, single-threaded for most tools, and uses .mxd documents rather than projects.

Esri ended support for ArcMap on 1 March 2026. It no longer receives fixes and will not open newer ArcGIS Pro formats, but a great deal of training material, older tutorials and departmental workflows in Pakistan were written for it, which is why some labs still have it installed. Learn it only if a course requires it; learn ArcGIS Pro for everything else.
A society mirror of the 10.8.2 installer will be added here. Until then, ask the GIS lab for the installation media.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (the application itself is 32-bit)
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended
About 5 GB of disk space
Microsoft .NET Framework 4.5 or later
A graphics card with 24-bit colour; 3D extensions need OpenGL 2.0
licensing: Needs a licence from the institute's education site licence, either an ArcGIS Administrator single-use authorisation or a concurrent licence from the lab's licence manager. Ask the lab coordinator.

name: ENVI
description: NV5's image analysis software, the standard commercial package for classification, spectral analysis and hyperspectral work.
about: ENVI (Environment for Visualizing Images) is built around the spectral side of remote sensing. It reads imagery from almost every satellite and airborne sensor, handles radiometric and atmospheric correction (FLAASH and QUAC), and offers a full workflow for supervised and unsupervised classification, change detection, spectral unmixing, target detection and hyperspectral analysis. Its feature extraction module does object-based segmentation and classification.

It runs on IDL, a scientific programming language, so every tool can be scripted, and newer versions also expose the ENVI API to Python. ENVI Modeler lets you chain tools into a reusable graph without code. Compared with SNAP or QGIS it is faster and better documented for spectral work, and it is the package most Pakistani remote sensing theses in the last two decades were produced with.
Version 6.5 is a 64-bit release with the modern workflow-based interface. The Deep Learning module is a separate licensed add-on and is not included.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; also available for Linux
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or more recommended for hyperspectral cubes
About 5 GB of disk space for the install; imagery needs far more
A graphics card with OpenGL 2.0 support; dedicated memory helps for large displays
Administrator rights for the installer and the licence tool
licensing: ENVI will not run without a licence. The institute's licence is served through the NV5 licence administrator; ask the remote sensing lab for the activation code or licence server address and enter it in the ENVI Licence Administrator after installing.

name: ERDAS IMAGINE 2025
description: Hexagon's image processing suite for photogrammetry, classification, orthorectification and large production workflows.
about: ERDAS IMAGINE is a raster-first remote sensing system that has been in production use since the 1980s. It covers image enhancement, mosaicking, orthorectification, pan-sharpening, classification (including the machine-learning operators added in recent versions), radar processing and terrain analysis. Spatial Modeler is its visual programming environment: tools are dragged into a graph, chained and run as batch processes on thousands of images.

Its photogrammetry side, IMAGINE Photogrammetry (formerly LPS), handles aerial triangulation, DEM extraction and orthophoto production for aerial and satellite stereo imagery, and is one reason survey organisations and mapping agencies use it. The 2025 release updates the interface, the sensor model library and the deep learning operators.

In Pakistan it is common in organisations that produce orthophotos and large mosaics, and in older remote sensing courses. ENVI is stronger for spectral analysis; IMAGINE is stronger for production and photogrammetry.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; Windows Server 2019 or later also supported
16 GB RAM recommended, 32 GB for photogrammetry and large mosaics
About 8 GB of disk space for the install, plus fast storage for imagery
A dedicated OpenGL 4.x graphics card with at least 4 GB of memory for stereo and 3D views
Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8 and Visual C++ runtimes, included with the installer
licensing: Licences are issued through the Hexagon Geospatial Licence Administration tool, either as a node-locked key or from the lab's licence server. Ask the remote sensing lab for the key or server address before installing; the installer alone does not run.

name: ArcGIS Reality Studio
description: Esri's photogrammetry application for turning aerial and drone imagery into true orthos, meshes, point clouds and surface models.
about: ArcGIS Reality Studio is a standalone photogrammetry application in Esri's ArcGIS Reality family. It takes large collections of overlapping images from drones, aircraft or satellites, runs aerial triangulation against ground control, and produces true orthophotos, digital surface models, dense point clouds and textured 3D meshes that load directly into ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online.

It is designed for city- and district-scale projects, so it is built to process tens of thousands of images on a workstation with a strong GPU and to produce outputs in Esri's scene layer formats. For small drone surveys, WebODM (free) or ArcGIS Drone2Map do the same job with far lower hardware demands; use Reality Studio when the project is large or when the deliverable must be an Esri mesh or scene layer.
Typical student uses are the campus 3D model, a true-ortho of a survey area, and comparing its surface model against GNSS check points.
requirements: Windows 11 or Windows 10 (version 22H2 or later), 64-bit
Eight or more processor cores; this is a workstation product
32 GB RAM minimum, 64 GB or more recommended
An NVIDIA graphics card with CUDA support and at least 8 GB of memory; more memory shortens mesh generation
Fast SSD storage: a medium drone project easily needs 100 GB of working space
Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime 8
licensing: Reality Studio is licensed as a user type extension on the university's ArcGIS Online organisation. Ask the GIS lab to assign the licence to your named-user account; without it the application opens but will not process.

name: GRASS GIS
description: Raster, vector and terrain analysis powerhouse. Also available inside QGIS through the Processing toolbox.
about: GRASS (Geographic Resources Analysis Support System) is the oldest open-source GIS still in active development and the one with the deepest raster and terrain toolset: hydrology (watersheds, flow accumulation, stream extraction), solar radiation, cost surfaces, landscape metrics, image classification and time-series modules. Everything is a command with documented parameters, which makes it natural to script in shell or Python.

It keeps data in its own location and mapset structure rather than opening files directly, which confuses first-time users but is what makes its analysis fast and its results reproducible. Most students meet it through QGIS, where the GRASS provider in the Processing toolbox exposes the same tools on ordinary files without the mapset setup.

Install it standalone when you need the full module set, large rasters, or the r.watershed and r.sim family of tools for hydrology and erosion modelling, which are the parts that have no equal in other free packages.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 11 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum; more for large DEMs
About 1 GB of disk space
On Windows, the standalone installer bundles Python and wxPython; the OSGeo4W installer is the alternative

name: SAGA GIS
description: Fast terrain and hydrological analysis with hundreds of modules, used in hydrology and geomorphology courses.
about: SAGA (System for Automated Geoscientific Analyses) is a lightweight GIS written for geoscientists. Its tool library is organised by theme: terrain analysis (morphometry, channels, hydrology, lighting), grid processing, geostatistics, image classification and climate tools. It is known for speed on large grids and for terrain indices (TWI, LS factor, curvature families, SAGA wetness index) that other packages lack or compute slowly.

The interface is plain, and SAGA uses its own grid format, but every tool is also available through the SAGA provider in QGIS Processing, where most students use it. Standalone SAGA is worth installing for terrain-heavy projects and for its tool chains, which can batch a whole terrain analysis from one dialog.
It has no licence cost, runs well on modest laptops, and is portable: unzip and run.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum
Under 500 MB of disk space; the Windows build is a zip that needs no installer
Microsoft Visual C++ runtimes, usually already present

name: ESA SNAP
description: The Sentinel Application Platform for processing Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery.
about: SNAP is ESA's free toolbox for the Sentinel missions and most other Earth observation sensors. It is the standard desktop tool for Sentinel-1 radar: calibration, speckle filtering, terrain correction, interferometry (InSAR) and polarimetry are all built in, and the processing graphs that do them can be saved and run in batch from the Graph Processing Tool.

For Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 it provides resampling, subsetting, band maths, indices, atmospheric correction through the Sen2Cor plugin, and a classification toolbox. Everything works on the .SAFE products you download from the Copernicus Data Space, with no conversion step.

SNAP is written in Java and feels slower than ENVI for display, but it is the only free package that covers the radar workflow end to end, which matters for flood mapping in the monsoon when optical imagery is cloud. The snappy and esa_snappy modules let you drive it from Python.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS or Linux, 64-bit
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended for Sentinel-1 interferometry
About 1 GB for the install; each Sentinel-1 scene is 4 to 8 GB, so plan for 50 GB or more of working space
Java is bundled with the installer; do not install it separately
A screen of at least 1280 x 800; the toolbox panels are dense

name: PostgreSQL with PostGIS
description: Spatial database for the database and web GIS courses. Install PostgreSQL, then add PostGIS from Stack Builder.
about: PostgreSQL is a general-purpose relational database, and PostGIS is the extension that teaches it geometry: spatial types, indexes, several hundred ST_ functions for measurement, overlay, buffering, routing with pgRouting, and raster storage. Together they are the back end of almost every serious web GIS and of most organisational data stores, and spatial SQL is the single most valuable skill in the GIS Analyst and GIS Developer roadmaps.

The workflow is: install PostgreSQL, run Stack Builder to add PostGIS, create a database, run CREATE EXTENSION postgis, and connect from QGIS, pgAdmin or Python. Data loads with the shp2pgsql tool, the QGIS DB Manager, or ogr2ogr. Queries that take minutes on shapefiles run in seconds once a spatial index exists.
Learn it with the PostGIS workshop linked above. The whole workshop runs on a laptop with the default install.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS or Linux
4 GB RAM is plenty for coursework; the server is light
About 1 GB of disk space plus your data
Administrator rights to install the Windows service
Remember the postgres superuser password you set during installation; it is needed for every connection

name: QField
description: Take a QGIS project to the field on Android or iOS. Offline capable, GNSS aware.
about: QField is the mobile companion to QGIS. You prepare a project on the desktop with the layers, forms, symbology and basemaps you want, copy it to the phone (or sync through QFieldCloud), and in the field you capture points, lines and polygons with the phone's GNSS or an external receiver, fill the same attribute forms, attach photos, and bring the edits back to QGIS.

It works fully offline, which matters in rural survey areas, and it supports external RTK receivers over Bluetooth for centimetre work. Field data collection with QField, a GeoPackage and an attribute form is the standard survey workflow in the Surveying and Precision Agriculture roadmaps.
Install it from the Play Store or App Store; the QField Sync plugin in QGIS packages the project.
requirements: Android 9 or later, or iOS 15 or later; a Windows build exists for tablets
A phone with GNSS and at least 3 GB RAM; a large basemap benefits from more storage
QGIS on the desktop with the QField Sync plugin to package projects
For sub-metre accuracy, an external GNSS receiver with Bluetooth

name: WebODM
description: Open-source drone image processing: orthomosaics, DEMs, point clouds and 3D models from UAV photos.
about: WebODM is the browser interface to OpenDroneMap, a free photogrammetry pipeline. Upload the photos from a drone flight, optionally add ground control points, and it runs structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo to produce an orthomosaic, a digital surface and terrain model, a dense point cloud and a textured mesh, with a viewer for each. Plant health indices and volume measurement are built in.

It runs as a set of Docker containers, so the free install on Windows means installing Docker Desktop with WSL 2 first and then running WebODM from a terminal. Processing is slow on a laptop (a 300-image flight can take an hour or more) but the results are comparable with Pix4D and Agisoft for mapping work, and the pipeline is fully documented.
The paid native Windows installer from the OpenDroneMap project is a convenience, not a different product. The Docker route is free.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 with WSL 2 and Docker Desktop, or macOS, or Linux (the simplest)
16 GB RAM recommended; 8 GB works for small flights with the split-merge option
A 64-bit processor; a GPU is optional and only speeds up part of the pipeline
20 GB free for the containers plus 5 to 10 times the size of your photos for working space
Virtualisation enabled in the BIOS for WSL 2

name: Google Earth Pro
description: Free desktop version with historical imagery, KML editing, and area and path measurement.
about: Google Earth Pro is the desktop edition of Google Earth and has been free since 2015. Its value to a GIS student is the historical imagery slider, which shows how a site has changed over twenty years of satellite and aerial images, and the ability to draw and measure placemarks, paths and polygons and save them as KML or KMZ for import into QGIS or ArcGIS.

It also imports shapefiles and GPS tracks, exports high-resolution images for reports, records tours, and shows 3D buildings and terrain. It is not an analysis tool and the imagery cannot be downloaded for processing, but for site reconnaissance, ground-truth planning and quick visual checks of a classified map it is used daily in practice.
Sign-in is not required.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 11 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM
About 2 GB of disk space for the install and cache
A graphics card with OpenGL or DirectX 9 support
An internet connection; imagery streams from Google and only a cache is stored locally

name: R and RStudio
description: R with the sf, terra and tmap packages for spatial statistics and publication-quality figures.
about: R is a programming language for statistics, and RStudio (from Posit) is the editor most people use it in. For spatial work the sf package handles vector data with the same simple-features model as PostGIS, terra handles rasters, tmap and ggplot2 make maps, and spdep, gstat and spatialreg cover spatial autocorrelation, interpolation and spatial regression. R is the standard tool for the statistical side of a thesis: sampling design, accuracy assessment, regression and figures that a journal will accept.

It overlaps with Python; Python is stronger for deep learning and for integration with GIS software, R is stronger for statistics, reproducible reports (Quarto and R Markdown) and plotting. Many researchers use both. The free book Geocomputation with R, linked above, is the complete course.
Install R first from CRAN, then RStudio. Packages install from inside R with install.packages().
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 12 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB for raster work with terra
About 1 GB for R and RStudio plus packages
On Windows, install Rtools as well if a package needs compiling

name: Pakistan administrative boundaries, including IIOJK
description: National, provincial, district and tehsil polygons that follow the official Survey of Pakistan map, with Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir included as its own feature. Shapefiles in WGS 84 with full metadata.
about: Most boundary files in circulation, GADM and the OCHA common operational datasets included, draw Pakistan without the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, or draw the Line of Control as if it were an international border. Any map made from them contradicts the official political map of Pakistan published by the Survey of Pakistan, which government departments, universities and most clients in the country expect. This dataset was created to fix that for student and research work.

Four shapefile layers, all in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326): National_Boundary with two features, Pakistan and IIOJK, so the outline can be drawn with or without the disputed territory; Provincial_Boundary with eight features (Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Gilgit Baltistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the Federal Capital Territory and IIOJK) with areas in square kilometres in geographic, UTM 41N and UTM 43N terms; District_Boundary with 161 districts; and Tehsil_Boundary with 554 tehsils.

The IIOJK polygon and the national and provincial outlines that include it were digitised by Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq against the Survey of Pakistan political map and merged with district and tehsil lines derived from the OCHA Pakistan and Population Census Organisation boundary data. Each layer carries the same metadata in ArcGIS (.shp.xml) and QGIS (.qmd) form, so the source, creator and licence travel with the file.
requirements: Any GIS that reads shapefiles: QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, GeoPandas, R sf
Reproject to UTM 42N (EPSG:32642) or a national equal-area projection before measuring areas; the stored areas were computed in UTM 41N and 43N
Districts reflect the 2017 census-era boundaries; districts created since then (for example in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan) are not split out
Cite as: Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq (2021), Pakistan administrative boundaries including IIOJK, Arid Society of GIS, with the OCHA/PCO base acknowledged

name: Galiyat boundary, Galiyat Development Authority jurisdiction
description: The Galiyat Development Authority's area of responsibility in Abbottabad district, from Murree Road through Ayubia, Nathia Gali and Thandiani, as one clean polygon. Shapefile in WGS 84 with metadata.
about: The Galiyat is the hill-station belt of Abbottabad district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Ayubia, Nathia Gali, Dunga Gali, Khaira Gali, Changla Gali, Bara Gali and Thandiani, on the ridge that runs north from Murree. Since 1996 it has been administered for planning, tourism, building control and services by the Galiyat Development Authority (GDA), a provincial body whose jurisdiction is a planning boundary rather than a tehsil or union council. Because it is not a census or revenue unit, it does not appear in the national administrative datasets, and anyone studying tourism, forest change, landslides or construction in the Galiyat has had to redraw it.

This file is that boundary as a single polygon of about 636 square kilometres with a perimeter of about 221 kilometres, in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The attribute table holds the name, authority, province, district, area, perimeter, source, creator and year, replacing the empty 27-field land use template the original digitising carried.

The boundary was digitised in May 2025 during the Galiyat land use survey against the GDA's notified limits and high-resolution imagery, and was cleaned, documented and published by Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq for the Arid Society of GIS. Metadata travels with the file in ArcGIS (.shp.xml) and QGIS (.qmd) form.
requirements: Any GIS that reads shapefiles: QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, GeoPandas, R sf
Use with the Pakistan administrative boundaries dataset above for tehsil and district context; the Galiyat crosses tehsil lines
Areas were computed on the WGS 84 sphere; reproject to UTM 43N (EPSG:32643) for engineering-grade measurements
This is the GDA jurisdiction, not the Ayubia National Park or the Galiyat forest division; those have their own, smaller boundaries
Cite as: Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq (2025), Galiyat boundary, Galiyat Development Authority jurisdiction, Arid Society of GIS

name: SRTM 30 m DEM, Pakistan mosaic
description: Void-filled SRTM 1 arc-second tiles mosaicked for the whole country, GeoTIFF, WGS84.

name: ESA WorldCover 10 m land cover, Pakistan
description: 2021 global land cover at 10 m clipped to Pakistan, with class legend and QGIS style file.

name: CHIRPS monthly rainfall, Pakistan, 1981 to 2025
description: Monthly precipitation rasters clipped to Pakistan, plus a district-level summary table.

name: OpenStreetMap roads and places, Pakistan
description: Roads, railways, waterways and populated places extracted from the Geofabrik Pakistan extract, GeoPackage.

name: WorldPop population 100 m, Pakistan 2020
description: Constrained population count raster, with district aggregates and 2023 census totals for comparison.

name: Society map layout template
description: QGIS print layout with the institute logo, north arrow, scale bar, legend and metadata block, A4 and A3.

name: Final year project report template
description: Word and LaTeX templates following the institute's formatting rules, with a sample chapter structure.
